messages.subject: Confusion over input for dDynOcc_ssm
parts:
Hi all,

Just had  question regarding some of the inputs/indexing used in nimbleEcology's dDynOcc (and perhaps related) distributions. For brevity, I have a model with a snippet of nimbleCode like :

for (s in 1:nsites){
      for (i in 1:nspec){
      y[s,1:NT,1:J,i]~dDynOcc_ssm(init=psi[i, s], probPersist=phi[i, s],
                           probColonize = phi[i, s], p=p[s,1:NT, 1:J,i],
                           start=Starts[s,1:2], end=Ends[s,1:2])
      }
    }

The sampling is ragged (hence the start/end declaration), and certain sites are not actually visited in certain primary periods. I've coded these with 0 Starts/Ends values, and left the corresponding y's for the upsampled primary/secondary occasions as NA (without providing initial values). If I'm following the function code for  dDynOcc_ssm correctly, it seems to me that the function can deal with upsampled primary periods: 

if (end[t] - start[t] + 1 > 0) {...
} else {
                if (t < nyears)
                  ProbOccNextTime <- ProbOccNextTime * probPersist +
                    (1 - ProbOccNextTime) * probColonize
            }
...etc. 

The model builds, compiles, etc., but when running, throws a number of errors regarding certain y logprobs being NA/NAN, and the samplers never update.

I'm having a little trouble finding direct reference to this in the documentation, but my intuition is that perhaps missing y's should be provided initial values,  that perhaps the indexing for y should exclude missing values, like

for (s in 1:nsites){
      for (i in 1:nspec){
      y[s, 1:NT, Starts[s, 1:2]:Ends[s, 1:2], i]~dDynOcc_ssm(init=psi[i, s], probPersist=phi[i, s],
                           probColonize = phi[i, s], p=p[s,1:NT, Starts[s, 1:2]:Ends[s, 1:2], i],
                           start=Starts[s,1:2], end=Ends[s,1:2])
      }
    }

or that perhaps start/end == 0 poses an issue? Realized that I don't have a strong sense of the function inputs (or whether missing observations must be imputed/sampled) across many of the nimbleEcology distributions, so just wanted to reach out before recreating the wheel or stumbling on a failed 'solution' that may not fail loudly.  

Thanks,

John

messages.subject: Re: Confusion over input for dDynOcc_ssm
parts:
Hi John,
It's a good point that this doesn't seem very clear.
I think the way it is written is that if you provide end[t] < start[t], that is interpreted as no-data for time t.
Does that work?
Perry
